Heading: Theme Author Guide
Starts at line: 1 (bounded excerpt)

# Theme Author Guide

This guide is for people who make or share their own themes. The first part walks you through your first theme with no coding experience needed. The rest is a reference: every colour, picture and part a theme can change, and the safety rules every theme follows. To pick, try, import or remove a theme, see [Custom CSS Themes](custom-css-themes.md).

**Token contract version 1** (`--mari-tokens-version: 1` on `:root`). The names in this guide keep working between releases. When one has to change, the version goes up and the change is listed under [Changes](#changes) at the end. Everything else (other `--ov-*`, `--mari-*` and `--marinara-*` variables, Tailwind classes, element structure) is internal and can change in any update.

## Your first theme, step by step

A theme is a short list of settings written in CSS, the language web pages use for colours and fonts. You don't need to know CSS to start. Each line looks like `--name: value;`: a **token** (a named setting that starts with `--`), a colon, the value, and a semicolon.

1. Open **Library → Settings → Appearance** and click **CSS Themes** in the row of sections.
2. To change a starter theme, download one you like from **Browse the theme gallery**, find it under **Starter themes** and click **Clone + Edit** (the copy icon). Marinara makes your own copy, named for example "Petal OS (my copy)", and opens it in the editor. Starter themes stay read-only, so the original is always there. To start from scratch instead, click **Create Theme**. Its template has lines between `/*` and `*/`, which are switched off. Delete those marks around a line to switch it on.
3. Type a name in the name box.
4. Change a colour. Find a line such as `--primary: #3fae7a;` and replace the colour. `#3fae7a` is a hex colour code. Any colour picker on the web gives you one. Names such as `teal` work too.
5. Leave **Preview** on. The app changes as you type, so you see each change at once.
6. Look under the editor. **No CSS problems found.** means the CSS is fine. Otherwise each problem shows with its line number, such as a missing `;` or `}`.
7. Click **Save**. Your new theme turns on, and Marinara asks **Keep this theme?** Click **Keep theme** within 15 seconds, or it goes back to your old look.

The tokens most people change first:

| Token            | What it colours                              |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `--background`   | The page behind everything                   |
| `--foreground`   | Main text                                    |
| `--primary`      | Buttons, links and highlights                |
| `--card`         | Cards and panels                             |
| `--sidebar`      | The chats and Library sidebars               |
| `--border`       | Lines around things                          |
| `--mari-font-ui` | The app font, for example `"Georgia", serif` |

A small theme:

```css
:root {
  --mari-tokens-version: 1;
  --primary: #3fae7a;
  --mari-selected-tint: var(--primary);
  --mari-font-ui: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
}

[data-theme="dark"] {
  --background: #0f1712;
  --card: color-mix(in srgb, #0f1712 80%, transparent);
  --sidebar: #0b120e;
}
```

`:root { … }` holds settings for every colour scheme. `[data-theme="dark"] { … }` holds settings for Dark only, and `[data-theme="light"] { … }` for Light only. To see the full list of tokens while you work, open **CSS Variable Reference** under the editor, or read [Colour tokens](#colour-tokens) below.

### Add pictures and fonts

Open **Pictures and sharing details (author, version, thumbnail, fonts)** under the editor and click **Add pictures**. Click a picture's name to put it in your CSS at the cursor. See [Pictures](#pictures) and [Backdrops](#backdrops) for where pictures can go.

Pictures and fonts must be inside the theme. A theme can't load anything from another website, so a link to a picture or a Google Font in your CSS won't work.

### Ask Professor Mari to make the art

If you have an image model set up in **Connections** (Codex, NovelAI, ComfyUI, an OpenAI image model and so on), Professor Mari can make a theme's pictures for you and put them in it. Ask her in plain words, for example "make my Harbor theme a night-sky backdrop" or "give the Home cards a brass frame".

1. Mari works on your own themes only. For a starter theme, click **Clone + Edit** first and ask her to work on the copy.
2. She writes the picture prompt herself and sends it to your image model exactly as written. Your image style profiles and prompt prefixes (usually set up for character art) are left out, so a backdrop doesn't come back as a portrait.
3. You see each picture before anything changes. Ask for a few versions to pick from (up to 4 at a time), or for fixes such as "crop it to the top half", "make the white background see-through" or "make it smaller". Each fix is a new version, and the earlier ones stay.
4. When you say yes, Mari saves the picture into your theme (as WebP, the same way **Add pictures** does) and puts it in the theme's CSS. It shows up under **Pictures and sharing details** like any picture you added yourself.

Each picture takes as long as your image model needs, often half a minute to a minute and a half. If your image connection uses your own ComfyUI workflow, text built into that workflow is still sent.

### Share your theme

1. In **Pictures and sharing details**, fill in **Author**, **Version** (such as `1.0`), **Description** and **Thumbnail**, and pick **Made for** (Dark, Light or both). To suggest your colours and font along with the theme, click **Use my current Appearance** under **Settings**. Save.
2. Click **Export** (the upload icon) on your theme's row. Marinara saves one `.json` file with the CSS, pictures and fonts inside.
3. If you used art or fonts someone else made, open the file in a text editor and add credits and a licence. See [Theme files](#theme-files).
4. Send that file. The other person imports it with **Import File** and sees your name, credits and a list of anything the theme changes before they install it.

### If something goes wrong

Marinara keeps the top bar, the sidebars, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> and the message box usable whatever a theme does. If your theme hides, moves or covers one of them, Save tells you what broke. You can still choose **Save anyway**, but Marinara switches the theme off in a tab as soon as it breaks one. To get your normal look back at any time, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> three times, add `?safe` to the end of the address, or press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> and type "Custom theme".

Starter themes are good examples to learn from. Clone one and read its CSS to see how it uses the tokens and part hooks below.

## How a theme wins

The app's own CSS sits in cascade layers, declared first thing in `index.html`:

```
mari-protected, mari-theme-important, theme, base, components, utilities, mari-app, mari-pickers
```

- A theme is **unlayered**, so a plain selector in a theme beats every app rule without `!important`,
  whatever the app rule's specificity.
- `mari-pickers` holds the Appearance pickers (background, accent, fonts, chat colours). It sits
  above the app's defaults and below a theme, so a theme's colours win over the pickers, and
  Appearance tells the user when a theme overrides a picker.
- `!important` in a theme still works. Those rules are copied into `mari-theme-important`, which
  beats the app's own `!important` rules.
- `mari-protected` keeps the top bar, the chats sidebar, the Library sidebar and Ctrl+K in place.
  A theme can restyle them (colours, fonts, borders, radius, shadows) but not hide, move, shrink or
  cover them. If it tries, the theme is switched off in that tab and the user is told why.

The way back always works: `?safe` in the URL, **Escape three times**, or Ctrl+K > "Custom theme"
turns the theme off. A new theme asks "Keep this theme?" and goes back after 15 seconds.

## Colour tokens

### Core (every visual style defines these)

`--background`, `--foreground`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`,
`--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--muted`,
`--muted-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground`,
`--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--radius`, `--sidebar`, `--sidebar-foreground`, `--sidebar-border`,
`--sidebar-accent`, `--sidebar-accent-foreground`.

Values are full CSS colours (`#1b1530`, `rgb(…)`, `oklch(…)`). Bare HSL triplets such as
`270 25% 8%` (the shadcn convention) are **not** valid here.

Scope light and dark separately with `[data-theme="light"]` and `[data-theme="dark"]`.

### New layout

| Token                                                            | Used for                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ov-line`                                                      | Hairlines and panel borders                                                                                                   |
| `--ov-text`, `--ov-muted`, `--ov-dim`                            | Text, secondary text, faint text                                                                                              |
| `--ov-accent`                                                    | Accent spots (defaults to `--primary`)                                                                                        |
| `--ov-hover`, `--ov-active-bg`                                   | Hover and pressed backgrounds                                                                                                 |
| `--ov-mode-conversation`, `--ov-mode-roleplay`, `--ov-mode-game` | Chat-mode colours in the chats sidebar and editors                                                                            |
| `--ov-serif`                                                     | Title font (follows `--mari-font-heading`)                                                                                    |
| `--mari-selected-tint`                                           | Selected rows, pills and toggles. Neutral (`--foreground`) by default; set it to `var(--primary)` for accent-tinted selection |
| `--mari-selected-bg`, `--mari-selected-ring`                     | Derived from the tint (10% and 18%)                                                                                           |

### Theme tokens (v1)

Each one defaults to the app's own look. Light mode has its own readable values.

| Token                                                                                                    | Used for                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mari-font-ui`                                                                                         | The whole app's font                                                                                                        |
| `--mari-font-heading`                                                                                    | Page and section titles                                                                                                     |
| `--mari-font-chat`                                                                                       | Message text in roleplay and conversation chats                                                                             |
| `--mari-mode-conversation`, `--mari-mode-roleplay`, `--mari-mode-game`                                   | Home chips, recent chats, the new-chat launcher, Home widget eyebrows                                                       |
| `--mari-home-pink`, `--mari-home-violet`                                                                 | The other Home widget accents                                                                                               |
| `--mari-status-online`, `--mari-status-idle`, `--mari-status-dnd`, `--mari-status-offline`               | Presence dots and labels                                                                                                    |
| `--mari-gauge-ok`, `--mari-gauge-warn`, `--mari-gauge-danger`                                            | Game gauges and HP bars. A widget's own colour still wins in its normal state; danger always uses the token                 |
| `--mari-game-combat`, `--mari-game-combat-text`                                                          | The game's Combat button                                                                                                    |
| `--mari-stage-empty-bg`                                                                                  | The game stage before a scene image loads (any `background`, gradients included)                                            |
| `--mari-scrim`                                                                                           | The dimmed backdrop behind Ctrl+K                                                                                           |
| `--mari-user-avatar-placeholder`                                                                         | Your avatar when you have no picture (a gradient)                                                                           |
| `--mari-art-saturation-1`, `--mari-art-lightness-1`, `--mari-art-saturation-2`, `--mari-art-lightness-2` | The gradient on cards without a picture. Each card keeps its own hue; set these (as percentages) to calm the gradients down |
| `--mari-app-backdrop`                                                                                    | An image or gradient behind the whole app, painted once (see below)                                                         |
| `--mari-accent-fx-animation`                                                                             | The Accent Pulse or RGB Mode animation while one is on, otherwise `none`                                                    |

### Theme tokens added in v1.1

These have no value until a theme sets one, so the user's own setting applies until then.

| Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Used for                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mari-text-outline`                                                                                                                                                                                                        | The outline on message text, for example `0` to turn it off or `1px #3b2a1a`. Otherwise it's the user's Text Outline setting
…

# Weather in Your Theme

When a story has weather, Marinara draws it over the chat: rain, snow, fog, falling leaves, petals, stars, a sun or a moon. Your theme can give all of it its own look. You can recolour the rain, make snow fall as pixel squares, swap leaves for pictures you drew, or turn your backdrop grey when it rains.

This guide walks you through it step by step. You need a theme of your own first. If you don't have one yet, the [Theme Author Guide](theme-author-guide.md) shows you how to make one in a few minutes. The [Weather](theme-author-guide.md#weather) section there is the short reference version of this page.

## How the weather works

The weather comes from the story. In a Roleplay or Game chat, the **World State** agent keeps track of the weather and the time of day, such as "heavy rain" and "night". Marinara reads those words and picks what to draw: rain streaks for "rain", flakes for "snow", stars and a moon for "night", and so on.

The app always does the drawing itself. Your theme doesn't draw anything. It sets a few `--mari-weather-` tokens (named settings, like `--primary`), and the app reads them and draws the weather your way. This keeps themes safe: nothing in a theme can run code, and the user's own settings, such as reduced motion, always win.

### Indoors the weather stays outside

When the story is inside, such as an inn, a bedroom or a World Maps room, the app doesn't rain across the whole screen. It keeps only the colour of the weather and the lightning flash, and the room stays dry. The app works out "inside" from the World State location ("Tideglass Inn, Brinewatch") or the World Maps place type. When it can't tell, the weather draws as usual. With **Weather Versions of Backgrounds** on (see [Roleplay Backgrounds](../roleplay/backgrounds.md#weather-versions-of-backgrounds)), the background picture itself shows the rain on the windows, and the moving weather comes back, drawn only on the window glass. Your theme's weather look applies there too.

### The weather with no theme

This is a rainy night with no theme: thin pale streaks over a dark blue wash. The pictures further down show the same chat with three starter themes.

## See the weather while you work

You don't need to wait for the story to rain. You can set the weather yourself.

1. Open **Library → Settings → Appearance** and check that **Dynamic weather effects** is on (under **Effects**) and **Reduce Ambient Animations & Effects** is off.
2. Open a Roleplay chat, then open **Chat Settings → Agents** and turn on **World State**.
3. Open the **World State** tracker. On a computer it's in the Tracker Panel. On a phone, tap the **World State** button.
4. Click the **Weather** value and type a weather word, such as `heavy rain`. Click **Time** and type `night`.
5. The weather starts at once. The chat now has its own tab in the top bar.

While you work on your theme, Settings fills the middle of the window and the weather pauses behind it. Save your theme, then click the chat's tab in the top bar to see the result. To try other weather, change the words in step 4. The table under **Which words make which weather** below lists them all.

> **Tip:** Lock the Weather value (lock mode in the tracker) so the AI doesn't change it while you test. See [Roleplay HUD and Trackers](../roleplay/hud-and-trackers.md).

## Your first weather look, step by step

Let's give the rain a colour and make the streaks longer, the way the NEON//GRID starter theme does.

1. Open **Library → Settings → Appearance → CSS Themes** and click **Edit theme CSS** (the code icon) on your theme.
2. Find the `:root {` line near the top of your CSS. If your theme doesn't have one, add `:root {` on a new line and `}` on the line after it.
3. Add these lines inside it, before the `}`:

```css
--mari-weather-rain-color: #3ff0ff;
--mari-weather-rain-length: 2.2;
--mari-weather-strength: 1.4;
```

4. Click **Save**. If Marinara asks **Keep this theme?**, click **Keep theme**.
5. Click your test chat's tab in the top bar. The rain is now cyan, the streaks are about twice as long, and they show more strongly.

What each line does:

- `--mari-weather-rain-color` is the colour of the raindrops. Any colour works: a hex code such as `#3ff0ff`, a name such as `skyblue`, or `rgb(63 240 255)`.
- `--mari-weather-rain-length` makes the streaks longer or shorter. `1` is normal, `2.2` is a bit more than twice as long.
- `--mari-weather-strength` makes every particle show more (above `1`) or less (below `1`).

### What you get

This is the same rainy night in NEON//GRID, which uses these three lines and a few more.

### Pick the colours for day and night

Colours that look good on a dark backdrop can vanish on a light one. Put day colours in a `[data-theme="light"]` block and night colours in a `[data-theme="dark"]` block, the same way you set any other colour:

```css
:root[data-theme="light"] {
  --mari-weather-rain-color: #1aa7c4;
  --mari-weather-snow-color: #22b8d6;
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --mari-weather-rain-color: #3ff0ff;
  --mari-weather-snow-color: #7af7ff;
}
```

## Which words make which weather

Each kind of weather has a short name. You use that name in the token, such as `snow` in `--mari-weather-snow-color`.

| When the story says                 | The app draws                                     | Name in the tokens                                         |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| rain, downpour                      | Rain streaks                                      | `rain`                                                     |
| storm, thunder, lightning           | Heavy rain with lightning flashes                 | `rain` (flash: `lightning-color`, bolts: `lightning-bolt`) |
| snow, sleet, blizzard, frost, cold  | Snowflakes                                        | `snow`                                                     |
| hail                                | Hailstones                                        | `hail`                                                     |
| fog, mist, haze                     | Soft fog banks low on the screen over ground mist | `fog`                                                      |
| sand, dust storm                    | Blowing sand                                      | `sand`                                                     |
| ash, smoke, volcanic                | Falling ash                                       | `ash`                                                      |
| fire, embers, inferno               | Rising embers                                     | `ember`                                                    |
| wind, breeze, gusts                 | Falling leaves                                    | `leaf`                                                     |
| cherry blossom, petals              | Falling petals                                    | `petal`                                                    |
| aurora, northern lights             | Aurora ribbons                                    | `aurora`                                                   |
| clear, sunny, cloudy, anything else | A few floating motes                              | `dust`                                                     |
| night (the time)                    | Stars and fireflies                               | `star`, `firefly`                                          |
| dusk, evening (the time)            | Fireflies                                         | `firefly`                                                  |
| morning, day, dusk (clear sky)      | The sun                                           | `sun`                                                      |
| night (clear sky)                   | The moon                                          | `moon`                                                     |

Stars skip foggy and snowy nights, and fireflies stay away from rain. The sun and moon only show when the sky is clear.

## Change colour, size and shape

Every kind in the table takes the same three settings. Put the kind's name in the middle of the token.

| Token                       | What it does                 | Values                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mari-weather-snow-color` | The colour                   | A plain colour: `#fff0f7`, `white`, `rgb(...)`, `hsl(...)` |
| `--mari-weather-snow-size`  | How big each particle is     | `0.5` (half) to `3` (three times)                          |
| `--mari-weather-snow-shape` | Round dots or little squares | `round` or `square`                                        |

Swap `snow` for any other name from the table, such as `--mari-weather-ember-color` or `--mari-weather-leaf-shape`.

Example: "data snow" for a computer-style theme, with small cyan squares instead of flakes.

```css
:root {
  --mari-weather-snow-color: #7af7ff;
  --mari-weather-snow-shape: square;
  --mari-weather-snow-size: 1.2;
}
```

Shapes don't apply to rain, fog or the aurora, which keep their own form. For fog, `--mari-weather-fog-color` tints both the drifting banks and the ground mist, and `--mari-weather-tint-strength` makes the mist thinner or thicker.

## Use your own pictures

Instead of dots and streaks, each kind can fall as pictures you made: maple leaves, sakura petals, paper stars, little pixel snowflakes.

1. Draw or find small pictures with see-through backgrounds, such as PNGs. Keep them small: a leaf about 24 to 64 pixels across is plenty. Anything bigger is shrunk to 160 pixels on its longest side.
2. In the theme editor, open **Pictures and sharing details** and click **Add pictures**. Add up to four pictures for one kind.
3. In your CSS, list them in the kind's `-image` token, with a space between each:

```css
:root {
  --mari-weather-leaf-image: url("theme:leaf-1.png") url("theme:leaf-2.png") url("theme:leaf-3.png");
  --mari-weather-leaf-size: 0.8;
}
```

4. Save, open your test chat and set its weather to `windy`. Your leaves now drift down, and each one picks one of your pictures.

Tips for pictures:

- Click a picture's name under **Pictures and sharing details** to put its `url("theme:...")` into your CSS at the cursor, so you don't have to type the name.
- A picture keeps the file name you added, ending and all, such as `leaf-1.png`. Use the name exactly as the list shows it.
- A picture is drawn with its own colours, so the `-color` token does nothing for that kind.
- Use `-size` to make all of them bigger or smaller. Smooth style also varies the size a little, so they don't all look the same.
- Leaves, petals and ash turn gently as they fall in smooth style. Other kinds stay upright.
- Pictures must be inside your theme. A link to a picture on another website is ignored.

The Lantern Path starter theme uses four painted leaves this way.

## Pixel style

Pixel style puts the whole weather layer on a grid of big square pixels, so it matches pixel-art themes. Raindrops, flakes and stars become crisp little blocks.

```css
:root {
  --mari-weather-style: pixel;
  --mari-weather-pixel-size: 3px;
  --mari-weather-petal-image: url("theme:wx-petal-1.png") url("theme:wx-petal-2.png");
  --mari-weather-petal-size: 3;
}
```

- `--mari-weather-style: pixel` turns pixel style on. `smooth` (or leaving it out) is the normal look.
- `--mari-weather-pixel-size` is how big each block is, from `2px` to `6px`. `3px` is a good start.
- In pixel style, your pictures are drawn at their own size times `-size`. Draw your pixel art at 1 pixel per art pixel, and set `-size` to the same number as the pixel size, so your art's pixels line up with the weather's. Petal OS draws 11-pixel petals at size `3`.
- In pixel style, pictures don't turn as they fall and are drawn solid (they fade in and out in three hard steps), so pixel art stays crisp.

### Example: Petal OS

This is the Petal OS starter theme on a blossom night. The petals are its own 11-pixel drawings, and the stars sit on the same 3 px grid.

## The sun and the moon

The sun and the moon take a colour, a size and one picture, like any other kind:

```css
:root {
  --mari-weather-sun-color: #ffe9a8;
  --mari-weather-moon-color: #ffe2f0;
  --mari-weather-moon-size: 1.5;
}
```

If your backdrop already has a painted moon, turn the app's moon off so there aren't two:

```css
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --mari-weather-moon: none;
}
```

`--mari-weather-sun: none` does the same for the sun.

## Calm it down or turn it up

These settings change the whole weather layer at once:

| Token                            | What it does                                                           | Values                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mari-weather-amount`          | How many particles fall                                                | `0.25` (a quarter) to `1` (normal). A theme can thin the weather out but never add more.              |
| `--mari-weather-speed`           | How fast things fall                                                   | `0.5` (half speed) to `1.5`                                                                           |
| `--mari-weather-strength`        | How strongly particles show                                            | `0.5` (faint) to `1.5` (bold)                                                                         |
| `--mari-weather-tint-strength`   | The coloured wash over the chat (blue in rain, dark at night)          | `0` (none) to `1` (normal)                                                                            |
| `--mari-weather-lightning-color` | The colour of the lightning flash                                      | A plain colour. The flash stays gentle and slow, so it's safe for people sensitive to flashing light. |
| `--mari-weather-lightning-bolt`  | Draws a forked lightning bolt with each flash, in the lightning colour | `on`, or a width from `0.5` to `3`. `none` (the default) keeps the flash only.                        |

For a quiet reading theme, try `--mari-weather-amount: 0.5;` and `--mari-weather-tint-strength: 0.3;`.

### Lightning bolts

By default a storm only flashes the screen. Add `--mari-weather-lightning-bolt` to draw a real forked bolt with each flash:

```css
:root {
  --mari-weather-lightning-color: #e8f2ff;
  --mari-weather-lightning-bolt: 1.2;
}
```

The bolt strikes down the left or right edge of the screen, never across the middle where the chat text is. It forks into several branches and glows in your lightning colour. It only shows while the app's own flash is up and fades with it, so a theme can't add flashes or make them faster. In pixel style the bolt is drawn in blocks on the pixel grid. Most starter themes use bolts: Apogee Lounge, Dewglass, Gutterlight, Under Sail and Velvet Casket. Granite Watch turns them off because it is set indoors.

## Make your backdrop follow the weather

Your theme's own art can change with the weather too. While a chat shows weather, Marinara adds two words to the page that your CSS can check:

- `data-mari-weather` is one of `clear`, `cloudy`, `rain`, `storm`, `snow`, `hail`, `fog`, `sand`, `ash`, `embers`, `wind`, `blossom` or `aurora`.
- `data-mari-sky` is one of `dawn`, `day`, `dusk` or `night`.

These are always one of the words above, never the story's own text. They go away when the chat has no weather or the user turns weather off.

Source: docs/appearance/theme-author-guide.md
Heading: Backdrops
Starts at line: 262


Set `--mari-app-backdrop` on `:root` to paint art behind the app:

```css
:root {
  --mari-app-backdrop: url("theme:city.webp");
  --mari-app-backdrop-position: bottom center;
  --mari-app-backdrop-rendering: pixelated;
}
```

It is drawn once, on its own fixed layer under the whole app (`[data-mari-part="app-backdrop"]`, so
Home's decorations and the light scheme never hide it), and it shows behind chats too: the roleplay,
conversation and game surfaces go transparent and the stock chat background steps aside. A
background the user picked for a chat still shows on top of it. Panels keep `--card` and
`--sidebar`, so make those translucent if you want the art to show behind them, and use
`--mari-page-veil` to tint full pages. To give pages a panel of their own, style
`[data-mari-part="page"]` (see Hooks): it holds every Library page, editor, Settings and Docs, so
Lorebooks gets the same panel as Characters.

| Token                            | Default                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mari-app-backdrop`            | One image or gradient                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--mari-app-backdrop-size`       | `cover` (try `auto` or `64px` for tiles)                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `--mari-app-backdrop-position`   | `center`                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `--mari-app-backdrop-repeat`     | `no-repeat`                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--mari-app-backdrop-attachment` | `fixed`                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--mari-app-backdrop-rendering`  | `auto` (`pixelated` for pixel art)                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--mari-app-backdrop-layers`     | A whole `background` value with several layers, such as `url(city.webp) bottom / 100% auto no-repeat, radial-gradient(#fff3 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 12px 12px, #fbe3ef`. It wins over the single-image tokens |

Custom images are the most flexible part of a theme: backdrops, a top bar strip, Home widget
frames and message frames (`border-image`, or a `background` on any part hook), tiled patterns
and bundled pixel fonts all ship inside the theme file, and the import preview lists them.
The user's Appearance > Accessibility > Theme art strength fades the backdrop and the ambient
overlay, and High contrast keeps them at 25% or less; a theme can't undo either.

data.output:
Source: docs/appearance/theme-author-guide.md
Heading: Theme tokens added in v1.1
Starts at line: 151 (bounded excerpt)


These have no value until a theme sets one, so the user's own setting applies until then.

| Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Used for                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mari-text-outline`                                                                                                                                                                                                        | The outline on message text, for example `0` to turn it off or `1px #3b2a1a`. Otherwise it's the user's Text Outline setting                                                                                                      |
| `--mari-dialogue-color`                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Dialogue colour when the character or persona has none of its own (their own colour still wins)                                                                                                                                   |
| `--mari-chat-font-size`                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Message text size. The Accessibility minimum still applies                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--mari-composer-placeholder`                                                                                                                                                                                                | The message box placeholder, as a quoted string: `"> waiting for user input..."`. Set it on `:root` or on one composer, such as `[data-composer="game"]`. Text that asks for keys or passwords is ignored                         |
| `--mari-page-veil`                                                                                                                                                                                                           | A colour laid over Settings, the Library, editors and Docs, so long text stays readable over a backdrop. `transparent` by default                                                                                                 |
| `--mari-top-bar-bg`                                                                                                                                                                                                          | A whole `background` value for the top bar: an image, a gradient or several layers. `--mari-top-bar-rendering: pixelated` keeps pixel art crisp. The tabs and icons always stay on top and visible                                |
| `--mari-top-bar-plate`, `--mari-top-bar-plate-radius`                                                                                                                                                                        | Over top-bar art, every tab, open-chat tab, icon button and the logo sits on a plate so it stays readable. These set the plate's colour and its corner radius (default `0.5rem`); set the radius to `0` for square pixel buttons. |
| `--mari-msg-head-rule`                                                                                                                                                                                                       | The line under the name in roleplay messages (a `border-bottom` value, such as `none` or `2px dashed currentColor`)                                                                                                               |
| `--mari-home-widget-border`, `--mari-home-widget-border-width`, `--mari-home-widget-radius`, `--mari-home-widget-bg`                                                                                                         | Every Home widget's frame and surface, Professor Mari included                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--mari-home-widget-font`, `--mari-home-widget-title-font`, `--mari-home-widget-title-size`, `--mari-home-widget-title-color`, `--mari-home-widget-eyebrow-size`, `--mari-home-widget-text-size`, `--mari-home-widget-muted` | Home widget type. Widgets grow taller when the text needs more room instead of clipping it                                                                                                                                        |
| `--mari-home-widget-eyebrow-color`, `--mari-home-widget-action-size`, `--mari-professor-sprite-scale`                                                                                                                        | The small label above widget titles, Professor Mari's Ask button text, and the size of Mari's picture (1 = stock)                                                                                                                 |
| `--mari-home-wash`                                                                                                                                                                                                           | The tint Home lays over a backdrop (stock: 65% of the card colour); `transparent` shows the art at full strength                                                                                                                  |
| `--mari-home-art`
